pages.text: "Heave! I'll push it!" Moya pressed their forehead to a huge fallen branch on the red dirt path. Overnight rain had brought it down. The waterhole sparkled beyond, and Moya wanted a drink now.
Tumba came up behind. "Shall I dig underneath?" "No, I'll do it alone!" Moya nudged Tumba away with their rump and pushed again.
The branch wouldn't budge. Three pushes only made Moya's hooves slide in the mud. Moya sat down, close to tears.
Tumba and Nia approached together. "Shall we push with you?" Nia asked. Moya hesitated, then nodded. "Can we... do it together?"

Nia looked down from their long neck. "It leans that way. Push from the same side! Tumba, underneath with your snout. Me, above with my head. Moya, the middle with your forehead!" Moya looked up. "That'll work!"
They lined up on one side. Nia called, "Push together, and it moves! One, two, three!" Heave! They pushed with all their strength.
Whoosh—the branch moved off the path! The red dirt way to the waterhole opened wide. Moya's neck straightened. "We did it!"
All three raced to the water and drank. Dripping, Moya said, "Alone it wouldn't budge. Together it slid right over!" Tumba puffed water from their snout.

Now Moya knew the steps. "One, ask for help when it's hard alone! Two, push from the same side! Three, count together!" Next day, a big stone blocked the path. Moya called first, "Push together, and it moves!"
By the waterhole, they touched noses. Tumba nuzzled Moya's side. "Together tomorrow, too!" Something that wouldn't budge for one moved for all. Push together, and it moves!
